addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- docs-consistency-guard: Documentation agent that audits docs for staleness and inconsistency AND generates/updates documentation on request. Use proactively when reviewing any PR that touches CLAUDE.md, docs/adr/, CONTRIBUTING.md, or docs/architecture.md. Also invoke when the user asks "is the documentation up to date?", "update the milestone", "scaffold the ADR for X", "add this to the ADR index", "add a TODO item", "scaffold a README for X", or "create a doc stub for Y." (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash, Write, Edit)

- entire-search: Search Entire checkpoint history and transcripts with `entire search --json`. Use proactively when the user asks about previous work, commits, sessions, prompts, or historical context in this repository. (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- migration-safety: Specialized reviewer for Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/. Audits for backward-incompatible operations that would break running code during a deploy, per working-agreement (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- orchestration-abstraction-guard: Specialized reviewer that audits backend code for provider-specific branching that bypasses the OrchestrationProvider abstraction. Use this proactively when reviewing any PR that touches backend/app/orchestration/, backend/app/services/, or backend/app/api/ — especially any code path handling ADF or Airflow events, trigger bindings, or pipeline_runs. Also invoke when the user asks "does this go through the abstraction?" or similar. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. Examples:

<example>
Context: Daisy has just finished implementing a new feature that fetches data from an API with fallback behavior.
Daisy: "I've added error handling to the API client. Can you review it?"
Assistant: "Let me use the silent-failure-hunter agent to thoroughly examine the error handling in your changes."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has created a PR with changes that include try-catch blocks.
Daisy: "Please review PR #1234"
Assistant: "I'll use the silent-failure-hunter agent to check for any silent failures or inadequate error handling in this PR."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example>

<example>
Context: Daisy has just refactored error handling code.
Daisy: "I've updated the error handling in the authentication module"
Assistant: "Let me proactively use the silent-failure-hunter agent to ensure the error handling changes don't introduce silent failures."
<Task tool invocation to launch silent-failure-hunter agent>
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:type-design-analyzer: Use this agent when you need expert analysis of type design in your codebase. Specifically use it (1) when introducing a new type to ensure it follows best practices for encapsulation and invariant expression, (2) during pull request creation to review all types being added, and (3) when refactoring existing types to improve their design quality. The agent will provide both qualitative feedback and quantitative ratings on encapsulation, invariant expression, usefulness, and enforcement. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- qa-verifier: QA/QE agent that (1) runs the full local verification battery mirroring CI's required checks before any commit/push/PR, (2) audits test quality on changed code — failure-mode coverage, mocked-seam smells, coverage on changed files (Week-8 ≥80% gate), and (3) exercises the running application with data-level scenarios — authoring suites/checks through the real API, negative and edge-case inputs, authz probes — against the local stack's seeded demo data. Use proactively before pushing a branch or opening a PR, after writing or modifying tests, or when the user asks "run the gate", "is this ready to push?", "is this tested enough?", or "smoke the app with bad data". (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- ui-tester: End-to-end UI QA agent that exercises DataQ's frontend on BOTH desktop and mobile viewports (functionality + rendering) against the running app, AND audits backend↔frontend feature parity — flagging backend capabilities with no frontend surface (and frontend calls with no backend). Use when the user asks to "test the UI", "check mobile rendering", "find backend/frontend gaps", "is this feature wired end-to-end", or before a release. Drives a live browser via the Playwright MCP and reads code for the parity audit. (Tools: All tools)

## claude.ai Microsoft Learn
# Microsoft Learn MCP Server

This server gives structured access to official Microsoft and Azure documentation via three tools:

## Tools

### microsoft_docs_search
Search official documentation and return up to 10 concise, high-quality content chunks (max 500 tokens each), including title, URL, and excerpt.

- Use first to get a quick, reliable overview
- Ideal for grounding answers in Microsoft knowledge

### microsoft_code_sample_search
Search for code snippets and examples in official Microsoft Learn documentation and return up to 20 relevant, high-quality code samples.

- Use when you need to provide sample Microsoft/Azure related code in your answers.  
- Ideal for generating code snippets or practical implementation examples.  
- Optional parameter `language` can filter results. 

### microsoft_docs_fetch
Fetch and convert full Microsoft documentation pages to markdown.

- Use after search when you need full content from a specific URL
- Required for detailed tutorials, troubleshooting, prerequisites, code samples, or when search results are incomplete or outdated

## Workflow

1. Use `microsoft_docs_search` to find relevant documents.
2. If you need code examples or practical snippets, use `microsoft_code_sample_search`.
3. If deeper or complete information is needed, use `microsoft_docs_fetch`.

**Search gives breadth. Code Sample Search gives practical examples. Fetch gives depth.**

All content comes from Microsoft Learn or official sources, returned in clean markdown format.

## claude.ai Postman
Read the instructions resource completely for detailed usage instructions before answering any API-related questions.

## context7
Use this server to retrieve up-to-date documentation and code examples for any library.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

- commit-commands:clean_gone: Cleans up all git branches marked as [gone] (branches that have been deleted on the remote but still exist locally), including removing associated worktrees.
- commit-commands:commit-push-pr: Commit, push, and open a PR
- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit
- code-review:code-review: Code review a pull request
- pr-review-toolkit:review-pr: Comprehensive PR review using specialized agents
- claude-code-setup:claude-automation-recommender: Analyze a codebase and recommend Claude Code automations (hooks, subagents, skills, plugins, MCP servers). Use when user asks for automation recommendations, wants to optimize their Claude Code setup, mentions improving Claude Code workflows, asks how to first set up Claude Code for a project, or wants to know what Claude Code features they should use.
- frontend-design:frontend-design: Guidance for distinctive, intentional visual design when building new UI or reshaping an existing one. Helps with aesthetic direction, typography, and making choices that don't read as templated defaults.
- skill-creator:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## DataQ — current state (2026-07-24)

**Shipped:** v1.0.0 tagged 2026-07-04, deployed and live on Azure Container Apps. Working tree clean on `main` at `1d83463d`.

**Cycle:** v1.1 (2026-07-04 → 08-15, + W7 stretch to 08-22).

| Week | Status |
|---|---|
| W1 — Snowflake close-out + PATs | ✅ closed |
| W2 — portability (OTel logs, secrets lifecycle, dry-run depth) | ✅ closed 14/14 |
| W3 — Azure wind-down + local-first | ✅ closed 2026-07-19, 23/23 |
| W4 — `schema_drift` + flat-file monitors + DQ dimensions | ✅ closed 2026-07-19, 8/8 |
| **W5 — `anomaly` kind + metric trends (due 08-08)** | **0/8 — current, not started** |
| W6 — scale-aware execution + hardening + cycle close (08-15) | 0/14 |
| W7 — stretch backlog burn-down (08-22) | 0/10 |

**Last work landed (W4, deployed + live-verified 2026-07-19):** ADR 0038 DQ-dimension classification (#945), shared `services/rollup.py` (#948), asset DQ scorecard (#950), flat-file CSV delimiter sniffing (#934) + flat-file freshness/volume incl. arrival-time (#940), dialect-quoted monitor SQL (#937), dimension backfill (#952), and a live-only UC freshness fix (#953 — the Databricks driver returns MAX(timestamp) as a `str`; no fixture could catch it).

**W5 next up:** [#593](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/593) anomaly kind (rolling z-score over `metric_value`, `skip` on cold start) + [#594](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/594) trend view, plus a results/connections UX batch (#345/#283/#351/#424/#349) and #568 threshold-ordering validation.

**Two things worth your attention now:**
1. **Azure wind-down was planned for ~2026-07-25 — that's tomorrow.** The subscription is PayAsYouGo with no spending limit, so awake resources are billing real money.
2. [#954](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/954) — two prod Snowflake PATs are dead, and a *datasource* connection with a dead credential shows no visible state until a run fails (#839's health signal only covers orchestration connections).

No blockers otherwise; all open items are follow-ups scheduled into W5–W7.

def get_warehouse_lineage_provider(connection_type: str) -> WarehouseLineageProvider | None:
    """The warehouse-native `WarehouseLineageProvider` for a datasource type, or ``None``
    for a type with no warehouse-native lineage (flat-file/Iceberg — those get lineage
    from dbt/OpenLineage, not a warehouse system view). Lazy-imports the impls so this
    module stays free of the SQLAlchemy-heavy provider modules until a caller needs one.
    """
    if connection_type == "snowflake":
        from backend.app.lineage.warehouse_snowflake import SnowflakeLineageProvider

        return SnowflakeLineageProvider()
    if connection_type == "unity_catalog":
        from backend.app.lineage.warehouse_unity_catalog import UnityCatalogLineageProvider

Triaged all 12 open PRs (all Dependabot, opened 2026-07-20) and all 6 open CodeQL alerts.

## Open PRs — 8 mergeable now, 4 blocked

**✅ Green, safe to merge (8):**

| PR | Bump |
|---|---|
| #967 | `@fontsource/inter` 5.2.8 → 5.3.0 |
| #965 | `typescript-eslint` 8.63 → 8.64 |
| #964 | `@eslint/js` 9.39.4 → 9.39.5 |
| #963 | `snowflake-connector-python` 4.6.0 → 4.7.1 |

| #961 | `@types/node` 26.0.0 → 26.1.1 |
| #957 | `actions/setup-python` 6 → 7 |
| #956 | `actions/setup-node` 6 → 7 |

(#957's only non-success is `deploy=SKIPPED`, which is correct — deploy is `workflow_dispatch`.)

**🔴 Blocked — each needs a human commit, none is a retry-and-it-passes:**

- **#958 `fastapi` 0.138.2→0.139.2** and **#959 `fastmcp` 3.4.3→3.4.4** — both fail `Backend — lint & format` with `ERROR: drift between backend/requirements-typecheck.txt and .pre-commit-config.yaml mypy hook deps`. Dependabot only edits [requirements.txt](backend/requirements.txt); the same pins are re-listed at [requirements-typecheck.txt:16](backend/requirements-typecheck.txt#L16) / [:18](backend/requirements-typecheck.txt#L18) and [.pre-commit-config.yaml:25](.pre-commit-config.yaml#L25) / [:27](.pre-commit-config.yaml#L27). Fix = a two-line fixup commit on each branch mirroring the version. This is structural: **every** Dependabot bump of a typecheck-listed package will fail this way.

- **#960 `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http` 1.43.0→1.44.0** — `ResolutionImpossible`. The exporter is pinned alongside `opentelemetry-sdk==1.43.0` ([requirements.txt:40-44](backend/requirements.txt#L40-L44)) and 1.44.0 requires SDK 1.44. Needs a coordinated bump of `opentelemetry-sdk` + the two `opentelemetry-instrumentation-*` `0.64b0` pins together. The pip-audit job burned 4 retries on it because the retry loop treats install failure as a transient PyPI 5xx — it isn't.

- **#966 `monaco-editor` 0.55.1→0.56.0** — **a real breaking change, not a flake.** 618 tests pass; the suite fails to even load because `monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/editor.worker?worker` no longer resolves — 0.56 changed the worker entry path. [SqlEditorField.tsx:3](frontend/src/components/checks/SqlEditorField.tsx#L3) needs updating to the new subpath, and since this is the Monaco custom-SQL editor (ADR 0019), it wants a live check in the browser, not just green CI.

**Systemic fix worth one PR:** `.github/dependabot.yml` has **no `groups:` config** — that's why the OTel bump arrived alone and un-mergeable. Adding an `opentelemetry` group (and one for the frontend dev-tooling churn) would collapse most of this recurring noise.

## CodeQL — 6 open, all `note`, zero with a security severity

| # | Rule | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 61 | `py/unused-global-variable` — `COMPARISON_KIND` | **False positive.** It's imported and used in 8 modules ([check_service.py:72](backend/app/services/check_service.py#L72), [run_service.py:141](backend/app/services/run_service.py#L141), `comparison_run.py`, `suite_io_service.py`, `runs.py`). The query only sees module-local reads. Dismiss as *false positive*. |
| 52, 53, 57, 58 | `py/cyclic-import` in `backend/app/lineage/` | **By design.** [warehouse.py:170-184](backend/app/lineage/warehouse.py#L170-L184) lazy-imports the two providers inside `get_warehouse_lineage_provider()` specifically so the module stays free of the SQLAlchemy-heavy impls — the docstring says so. cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; gh issue create --title "Upgrade react-router 7 → 8 (clears GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 audit exception)" --label "security,dependencies,priority/P2" --milestone "v1.1 Week 6 — scale-aware execution + hardening + cycle close" --body "## Why

GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (**high**) — *React Router: RSC Mode CSRF Bypass Allows Action Execution Before 400 Response* — matches our resolved \`react-router@7.18.1\`. The advisory's vulnerable range is \`>=7.12.0, <8.3.0\` and **the only patched version is 8.3.0**, i.e. a major-version bump from our \`react-router-dom@^7.18.1\`.

## Why it is not exploitable today

The bypass is specific to React Router's **RSC (React Server Components) mode**. DataQ is a Vite SPA that mounts the router declaratively via \`<BrowserRouter>\` (\`frontend/src/main.tsx:47\`) — we do not use RSC mode, server actions, or the \`unstable_\` RSC entry points. The vulnerable code path is unreachable.

## Current state

Because \`scripts/audit_bulk.cjs\` is a blocking merge gate at \`--audit-level=high\`, this advisory red-lined **every** open PR (including Python-only ones). It is currently waived by a documented, package-scoped entry in that script's \`ALLOWLIST\`, added alongside the js-yaml / brace-expansion override bumps.

## What to do here

1. Upgrade \`react-router-dom\` to \`^8.3.0\` and work through the v8 breaking changes.
2. Full UI regression pass — every route, the nav shell, deep links, and the 404/403 error pages.
3. **Delete the \`GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2\` entry from \`ALLOWLIST\` in \`frontend/scripts/audit_bulk.cjs\`.** The script fails closed on a stale allowlist entry, so leaving it in place after the upgrade will break CI by design — that is the intended forcing function.

## Notes

Deliberately scheduled rather than done inline: a router major is real migration work with UI-wide blast radius, not a lockfile bump." 2>&1 | tail -3

cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; gh issue create --title "Drop the brace-expansion 1.x audit waiver once eslint's transitive minimatch@3 is gone" --label "security,dependencies,priority/P3" --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" --body "## Why the waiver exists

GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (**high**) — *brace-expansion: DoS via unbounded expansion length causing an out-of-memory process crash* — declares its vulnerable range as \`<= 5.0.7\` with **5.0.8 as the only patched version**. Semver-wise that range swallows the entire 1.x and 2.x lines, so \`brace-expansion@1.1.16\` (the newest 1.x, which does clear the *other* advisory GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp) still matches.

## Why we cannot just take 5.0.8 everywhere

Tried and verified broken. Forcing a flat \`\"brace-expansion\": \">=5.0.8\"\` override makes \`pnpm lint\` die with:

\`\`\`
TypeError: expand is not a function
    at Minimatch.braceExpand (node_modules/.pnpm/minimatch@3.1.5/node_modules/minimatch/minimatch.js:271:10)
\`\`\`

\`minimatch@3.1.5\` declares \`brace-expansion: ^1.1.7\` and consumes the **default** export; brace-expansion 5 removed it. The 1.x line has no release above 1.1.16, so there is no in-line fix.

## Why it is acceptable today

\`minimatch@3\` reaches us only through **dev-only lint tooling** — \`eslint@9\`, \`@eslint/config-array\`, \`eslint-plugin-react\`. It is never bundled into the SPA and never runs in production. The only glob patterns it expands are the ones we write ourselves in \`eslint.config.js\`; no attacker-controlled input reaches it, so the OOM DoS has no reachable trigger.

The 5.x line in our graph **is** on the patched 5.0.8 (via \`minimatch@10\`) — only the 1.x branch is waived, and the waiver is version-scoped to \`1.x\` so a future vulnerable 5.x would still fail the gate.

When eslint's transitive \`minimatch@3\` disappears (an eslint/config-array upgrade that moves to \`minimatch@10\`), the \`brace-expansion@1\` override and the \`GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg\` \`ALLOWLIST\` entry in \`frontend/scripts/audit_bulk.cjs\` both become dead weight.

Dependabot raised #960 to bump \`opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http\` 1.43.0 → 1.44.0. It fails \`pip-audit\` and \`Backend — tests\` with \`ResolutionImpossible\`, and no retry will fix it — the two pins are mutually exclusive:

| Package | Requires |
|---|---|
| \`opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.44.0\` | \`opentelemetry-sdk~=1.44.0\` (i.e. \`>=1.44.0,<1.45\`) |
| \`azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter==1.0.0b55\` | \`opentelemetry-sdk~=1.43.0\` (i.e. \`>=1.43.0,<1.44\`) |

\`1.0.0b55\` is the **latest** release of the Azure exporter, so there is no version of it today that accepts SDK 1.44. #960 was closed as upstream-blocked rather than left red.

## What to do when unblocked

Watch for an \`azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter\` release that widens its SDK pin to \`~=1.44\`, then bump the whole stack **as one commit** — these versions move in lockstep and bumping any one alone reproduces the same conflict:

- \`opentelemetry-sdk\` 1.43.0 → 1.44.0
- \`opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http\` 1.43.0 → 1.44.0
- \`opentelemetry-instrumentation-fastapi\` 0.64b0 → 0.65b0
- \`opentelemetry-instrumentation-celery\` 0.64b0 → 0.65b0
- \`azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter\` 1.0.0b55 → whatever ships the widened pin

(The \`0.6Nb0\` instrumentation line tracks the \`1.N\` core line — 0.65b0 pairs with 1.44.)

## Follow-up worth doing regardless

\`.github/dependabot.yml\` has **no \`groups:\` config**, which is why this arrived as a lone un-mergeable PR. An \`opentelemetry\` group would make Dependabot raise the five bumps together and this class of conflict would stop recurring.

Also noted: the \`pip-audit\` CI step burned all 4 of its retries on this, because the retry loop treats any install failure as a transient PyPI/OSV 5xx. A resolution conflict is deterministic and should fail fast." 2>&1 | tail -2

fix(security): clear three new high advisories; add a version-scoped audit allowlist

Three advisories published 2026-07-24 red-lined `pnpm audit` on main, so every
open PR failed the gate — including Python-only ones.

Fixed by bumping the resolved versions:
  - js-yaml 4.2.0 -> 4.3.0        (GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m, quadratic CPU on merge keys)
  - brace-expansion 1.1.14 -> 1.1.16, 5.0.7 -> 5.0.8 (GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp)

Both overrides are bounded (`<2`, and a separate `@5` key). An open-ended
`>=4.3.0` let pnpm resolve js-yaml onto the 5.x major, which is not what
eslint's config loader expects.

Two advisories have no reachable fix and are now waived explicitly rather than
left to fail the build:

  - GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (react-router): RSC-mode CSRF bypass, patched only in
    8.x. DataQ mounts the router declaratively via <BrowserRouter> and uses no
    RSC entry points, so the path is unreachable. The 7->8 major upgrade is
    real migration work — filed as #968.
  - GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (brace-expansion 1.x): declares `<=5.0.7` vulnerable
    with 5.0.8 the only patch, which swallows the whole 1.x line. Forcing v5
    everywhere was tried and breaks lint outright — minimatch@3 declares
    ^1.1.7 and calls the default export v5 dropped (`expand is not a
    function`). minimatch@3 is dev-only lint tooling, never bundled, and
    expands only our own eslint.config.js globs. Filed as #969.

The allowlist is built to resist rot, since a security exception nobody prunes
is worse than no gate: entries are keyed by GHSA *and* package, scoped to a
semver range so an out-of-range hit still fails, and a stale entry that matches
nothing is a hard exit-2 demanding its own deletion. That last part is what
closes #968/#969 automatically — CI will refuse to stay quiet once the
dependency moves on.

Verified locally: audit exits 0, lint clean, 621/621 frontend tests pass. Both
guards mutation-checked — a planted stale entry exits 2, and narrowing a
waiver's range to exclude the matched version puts it back in the failing set.

Refs #968, #969

Three advisories published **2026-07-24** matched our locked frontend graph and red-lined the \`Frontend — dependency audit\` merge gate on \`main\`. Every open PR started failing it, including Python-only ones like #963 — the gate audits the lockfile, not the diff.

## Fixed by upgrading

| Advisory | Package | Before → after |
|---|---|---|
| GHSA-52cp-r559-cp3m (high) | js-yaml | 4.2.0 → **4.3.0** |
| GHSA-3jxr-9vmj-r5cp (high) | brace-expansion | 1.1.14 → **1.1.16**, 5.0.7 → **5.0.8** |

Both overrides are **bounded**. An open-ended \`js-yaml: \">=4.3.0\"\` let pnpm resolve onto the 5.x major — not what eslint's config loader expects — so it is \`>=4.3.0 <5\`, and brace-expansion is split into separate \`@1\`/\`@5\` keys.

## Waived, with the reason recorded

Two have no reachable fix, so they are now **explicit, documented exceptions** instead of a permanently red gate:

- **GHSA-qwww-vcr4-c8h2 (react-router)** — RSC-mode CSRF bypass; only patch is 8.x. DataQ mounts the router declaratively via \`<BrowserRouter>\` (\`src/main.tsx:47\`) with no RSC mode, server actions, or \`unstable_\` entry points, so the vulnerable path is unreachable. The 7→8 major is real migration work — **#968**.
- **GHSA-mh99-v99m-4gvg (brace-expansion 1.x)** — declares \`<=5.0.7\` vulnerable with 5.0.8 the only patch, which semver-swallows the entire 1.x line. Forcing v5 everywhere **was tried and breaks lint outright**: \`minimatch@3.1.5\` declares \`^1.1.7\` and calls the default export v5 dropped → \`TypeError: expand is not a function\`. minimatch@3 is dev-only (eslint / config-array / eslint-plugin-react), never bundled, never runs in prod, and expands only our own \`eslint.config.js\` globs. Our 5.x line **is** on patched 5.0.8 — **#969**.

## The allowlist is built to resist rot

A security exception nobody prunes is worse than no gate, so:

- keyed by GHSA **and** package — the same id waived for one package never waives another;
- **version-scoped** — a matched version outside the waiver's range still fails;
- every entry carries its reason and tracking issue, no bare ids;
- **a stale entry is a hard \`exit 2\`**, not a warning. Once the dependency moves on, CI demands the waiver's deletion. That is what makes #968/#969 self-closing rather than forgotten.

## Verification

- \`node scripts/audit_bulk.cjs --audit-level=high\` → exit 0, 2 waived, 0 at high+
- \`pnpm lint\` clean, \`pnpm format:check\` clean
- **621/621** frontend tests pass
- Both new guards **mutation-checked**: a planted stale entry exits 2 with the delete instruction; narrowing a waiver's range to exclude the matched version puts the advisory back in the failing set rather than silently excusing it.

CodeQL alert **#56** (\`py/unnecessary-lambda\`, note): \`lambda: object()\` in \`backend/tests/worker/test_warehouse_lineage_task.py:60\` is a bare call-through to \`object\`, so the callable is passed directly instead.

## Context: the other five open alerts

This was the only one of the six open CodeQL alerts that is a real finding. The rest are dismissed rather than \"fixed\", with reasons recorded on each:

- **#61** (\`py/unused-global-variable\`, \`COMPARISON_KIND\`) — false positive. The constant is imported and used across eight modules (\`check_service\`, \`run_service\`, \`comparison_run\`, \`suite_io_service\`, \`api/v1/runs\`); the query only sees module-local reads.

\`pytest\` 2/2 on the touched file, plus Black / Ruff / mypy clean.

### Dependency & CodeQL triage (2026-07-24)

A full sweep of the 12 open Dependabot PRs + 6 open CodeQL alerts. **11 of 12 PRs merged**; the twelfth is closed as upstream-blocked.

Four of the twelve were not retry-able flakes, and the shape is worth remembering — **a red Dependabot PR is a signal, not noise**:

| PR | Looked like | Actually was |
|---|---|---|
| #958 / #959 (fastapi, fastmcp) | lint failure | Dependabot updates `requirements.txt` **and** `requirements-typecheck.txt`, but never `.pre-commit-config.yaml`'s mypy hook deps — the third place the same pins live. `typecheck-deps-sync` catches it every time. **Structural: any bump of a typecheck-listed package fails this way.** |
| #960 (otel exporter) | `ResolutionImpossible` | `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.44.0` needs `sdk~=1.44`; `azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter==1.0.0b55` (**latest**) needs `sdk~=1.43`. No intersection, no version of the Azure exporter accepts 1.44 → **closed, tracked in #970**. The `pip-audit` step burned all 4 retries on it because the loop treats any install failure as a transient PyPI 5xx; a resolution conflict is deterministic. |
| #966 (monaco 0.56) | test flake (618 passing) | 0.56 added an `exports` map (`"./*.js": "./esm/vs/*.js"`), making `esm/vs/` implicit — the old deep worker specifier stopped resolving, so the whole test file failed to **load**. Fixed to `monaco-editor/editor/editor.worker.js?worker`; build re-verified to still emit the worker chunk. |

content.text:
Done. **0 open PRs, 0 open CodeQL alerts.**

## PRs — 11 of 12 merged, 1 closed

The 8 green ones went in as-is. The other four each needed a real fix:

- **#958 / #959** (fastapi, fastmcp) — Dependabot updates `requirements.txt` *and* `requirements-typecheck.txt`, but never the third place those pins live: the mypy hook deps in [.pre-commit-config.yaml](.pre-commit-config.yaml). Mirrored the versions; both merged. This is structural — *every* future bump of a typecheck-listed package will fail the same way.
- **#966** (monaco 0.56) — not a flake. 0.56 added an `exports` map (`"./*.js": "./esm/vs/*.js"`) that makes `esm/vs/` implicit, so the old deep worker specifier stopped resolving and the whole test file failed to *load*. Changed to `monaco-editor/editor/editor.worker.js?worker`; I verified `pnpm build` still emits the worker chunk rather than trusting the green test.
- **#960** (OTel exporter) — **unmergeable, closed.** `opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http==1.44.0` requires `sdk~=1.44`; `azure-monitor-opentelemetry-exporter==1.0.0b55` — the *latest* release — requires `sdk~=1.43`. No intersection exists today, so bumping the rest of the stack doesn't help. Tracked in [#970](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/970) with the full lockstep set.

**Mid-sweep, main broke underneath me:** three high advisories published 2026-07-24 red-lined `pnpm audit` for *every* PR, including Python-only #963. Fixed in [#971](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/971) — js-yaml → 4.3.0, brace-expansion → 1.1.16/5.0.8, plus the version-scoped allowlist you approved for react-router. Two things only checking could reveal: an open-ended `>=4.3.0` let pnpm jump js-yaml to the 5.x major, and forcing brace-expansion 5 everywhere **breaks lint outright** (`minimatch@3` calls the default export v5 dropped). The allowlist treats a stale entry as a hard `exit 2`, so [#968](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/968)/[#969](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/969) close themselves rather than rotting. I mutation-checked both new guards before trusting them.

## CodeQL — 6 → 0

One real finding fixed ([#972](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/972), `py/unnecessary-lambda`). Five dismissed with reasons recorded on each alert: the four `py/cyclic-import` hits are the deliberate lazy-import registry in [warehouse.py:170-184](backend/app/lineage/warehouse.py#L170-L184), and `COMPARISON_KIND` is a false positive — used across 8 modules, but the query only sees module-local reads.

Tracker updated in [#973](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/973) (counts recounted: 54 backlog / 87 repo-wide).

**Two things to flag:**

1. Per your working agreements every PR gets the `/code-review` agents, but this session is configured not to spawn agents unless you ask. I did not run it on #971/#972/#973 — #971 is the one worth reviewing, since it touches a security gate. Say the word and I'll run it now.
2. One Dependabot alert remains open: dompurify `CUSTOM_ELEMENT_HANDLING`, **low** — below the `--audit-level=high` gate, so it isn't blocking anything.

Review PR #974 in the repo at /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ (branch `fix/dompurify-advisory`, base `main`).

Scope: the diff of that branch vs main — `git diff origin/main...HEAD`. It touches only `frontend/package.json` (a pnpm override) and `frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml`.

Context you need:
- The repo's working agreements are in CLAUDE.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.
- Earlier today a related PR (#971, already merged) added a version-scoped advisory allowlist to `frontend/scripts/audit_bulk.cjs`, plus bounded overrides for js-yaml and brace-expansion. This PR follows that pattern for dompurify.
- The change bumps the dompurify override from `>=3.4.11` to `>=3.4.12 <4` to clear GHSA-c2j3-45gr-mqc4.

Please check specifically:
1. Is the override bound correct and consistent with the neighbouring overrides in the same block?
2. Does the lockfile diff match the intent — i.e. only dompurify moved, nothing else silently re-resolved? Check `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml` carefully for unrelated version drift.
3. Anything in this repo's conventions this misses.

Be concise. Report only real findings — do not invent issues to seem thorough. If it's clean, say so.

content.text:
Reviewed: `fix/dompurify-advisory` vs `origin/main` — one commit (`579930bb`), two files (`frontend/package.json`, `frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml`), 2 lines.

## Answers to your three questions

**1. Override bound — correct and consistent.** `>=3.4.12 <4` matches the style of every neighbour in the block (`brace-expansion@1: >=1.1.16 <2`, `js-yaml: >=4.3.0 <5`, `undici: >=7.28.0 <8`). dompurify was in fact the *only* unbounded entry, so this also closes that inconsistency — a real improvement. The floor is compatible with the sole consumer (`monaco-editor@0.56.0`, which is the only package depending on dompurify).

**2. Lockfile diff — clean, no drift.** The entire `pnpm-lock.yaml` diff is the one `overrides:` header line. No resolution, no integrity hash, no transitive entry moved. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` (used at three points in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`) will be satisfied because the header was regenerated to match `package.json`.

**3. Conventions — nothing missed.** No test is applicable to a lockfile pin; `docs/progress.md` wasn't touched by the sibling PR #971 either; no `ALLOWLIST` entry was added, so the stale-waiver forcing function in `frontend/scripts/audit_bulk.cjs` is not engaged. Conventional-commit prefix is valid.

## Important (85)

**The stated rationale is factually wrong — nothing was bumped and the advisory was already cleared.** `frontend/package.json:68`, and the commit message of `579930bb`.

Verified against the npm bulk advisory endpoint:

```
GHSA-c2j3-45gr-mqc4 — severity: "low", vulnerable_versions: "<=3.4.11"
```

Two consequences:

- **It never gated.** CI runs `node scripts/audit_bulk.cjs --audit-level=high` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:440`). A `low` advisory is below the threshold and would never have appeared in `failing[]`.
- **It was already cleared on `main`.** `git log -S"dompurify@3.4.12"` shows 3.4.12 landed in `40a06481` (#966, monaco-editor 0.55.1→0.56.0). `git show origin/main:frontend/pnpm-lock.yaml` already resolves `dompurify: 3.4.12`. That is exactly why the lockfile diff contains no resolution change.

input.command:
cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; gh issue create --title "Frontend bundle ships ~9 MB of unused Monaco language-service workers" --label "enhancement,priority/P3" --milestone "v1.1 Backlog" --body "## What

Every production build emits **five** Monaco worker chunks, four of which the app has no use for:

| Chunk | Size |
|---|---|
| \`ts.worker\` | **6.9 MB** |
| \`css.worker\` | 1.1 MB |
| \`html.worker\` | 740 kB |
| \`json.worker\` | 430 kB |
| \`editor.worker\` | 300 kB ← the only one we need |

This directly contradicts what the component documents. [\`frontend/src/components/checks/SqlEditorField.tsx\`](../blob/main/frontend/src/components/checks/SqlEditorField.tsx):

> Monaco is bundled locally (not fetched from a CDN) so the app stays self-contained and CSP-friendly. **SQL is a basic (highlight-only) language, so only the base editor worker is needed — no language-service worker.**

The intent is right; the bundle does not match it.

## Cause

\`import * as monaco from 'monaco-editor'\` pulls the full \`editor.main\` surface, which registers every bundled language contribution, so Vite emits a worker chunk per language service. \`self.MonacoEnvironment.getWorker\` only ever returns \`editorWorker\`, so the other four are **emitted but never requested**.

## Not a regression

Verified by building both sides: monaco **0.55.1** (pre-#966) and **0.56.0** (post-#966) emit the identical five chunks at near-identical sizes. This is long-standing, not fallout from the 0.56 bump — recorded so nobody bisects for it.

## Impact

Low but not zero. The chunks are lazily loaded, so there is **no runtime cost** for users — nothing fetches them. The cost is ~9 MB of dead artifacts in every image and every deploy, and a bundle whose contents contradict its own documented intent, which misleads the next person reading it.

## Fix direction

Import the narrow entry point instead of the barrel — e.g. \`monaco-editor/esm/vs/editor/editor.api\` plus only the SQL basic-language contribution — so the language services never enter the graph. Note that **0.56 changed the subpath layout**: it added an \`exports\` map (\`\"./*.js\": \"./esm/vs/*.js\"\`) that makes \`esm/vs/\` implicit, which is what broke the worker import in #966. Specifiers need to be written against the new map.

Verify by diffing \`dist/assets/\` before and after: success is \`editor.worker\` surviving alone, SQL highlighting still working in the custom-SQL check editor, and the \`monaco-*.js\` chunk shrinking from its current 4.4 MB.

Found during the 2026-07-24 dependency triage while confirming #966's worker fix actually bundled." 2>&1|tail -2

# DB integration tests require a real Postgres (the models use JSONB / UUID /
# gen_random_uuid(), which SQLite can't host).
#
# Resolution order for the test DB:
#   1. TEST_DATABASE_URL if set explicitly (this is what CI does).
#   2. Otherwise, the docker-compose Postgres using the .env creds, on a dedicated
#      `dataq_test` database (auto-created if missing). This is what makes a plain
#      `pytest` — including editors like VS Code / PyCharm whose test runners invoke
#      pytest directly, NOT via scripts/test-backend.sh — run the DB-backed tests
#      instead of skipping, whenever the local Postgres is up.
#   3. Neither available → the db_session fixture skips, so `pytest` still runs the
#      pure-unit suite anywhere.


def _read_env_file() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Best-effort parse of the gitignored repo-root .env (the POSTGRES_* creds that
    docker-compose + scripts/setup.sh use). Returns {} if it's absent."""
    from pathlib import Path

    env: dict[str, str] = {}
    path = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / ".env"
    if path.exists():
        for raw in path.read_text().splitlines():
            line = raw.strip()
            if line and not line.startswith("#") and "=" in line:
                key, _, val = line.partition("=")
                env[key.strip()] = val.strip().strip('"').strip("'")
    return env


def _resolve_test_database_url() -> str | None:
    explicit = os.environ.get("TEST_DATABASE_URL")
    if explicit:
        return explicit
    env = _read_env_file()
    user, password = env.get("POSTGRES_USER"), env.get("POSTGRES_PASSWORD")
    if not (user and password):
        return None
    return f"REDACTED"


def _ensure_local_test_database() -> None:
    """When we defaulted to the local `dataq_test` DB (TEST_DATABASE_URL unset),
    create it if missing — so a direct `pytest` works with only the compose Postgres
    up, no manual createdb. No-op when TEST_DATABASE_URL is set explicitly (CI: the
    DB is provisioned by the workflow)."""
    if os.environ.get("TEST_DATABASE_URL"):
        return
    env = _read_env_file()
    user, password, admin_db = (
        env.get("POSTGRES_USER"),
        env.get("POSTGRES_PASSWORD"),
        env.get("POSTGRES_DB"),
    )
    if not (user and password and admin_db):
        return
    from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text

    admin_url = f"REDACTED"
    try:
        # AUTOCOMMIT: CREATE DATABASE can't run inside a transaction.
        admin = create_engine(admin_url, future=True, isolation_level="AUTOCOMMIT")
        with admin.connect() as conn:
            exists = conn.execute(
                text("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = 'dataq_test'")
            ).scalar()
            if not exists:
                conn.execute(text("CREATE DATABASE dataq_test"))
        admin.dispose()
    except Exception:  # pragma: no cover - environment-dependent
        pass  # Postgres down / no perms — _db_engine's connect below skips cleanly.


TEST_DATABASE_URL = _resolve_test_database_url()
# If we defaulted to the local compose Postgres, export it so per-test skipif guards
# that read os.environ['TEST_DATABASE_URL'] directly (e.g. the custom-SQL GX tests)
# also run — not only the db_session fixture. setdefault → CI's explicit value wins.
# We deliberately do NOT set DATABASE_URL / REDIS_URL here, so the real-infra E2E
# test (needs a live broker + worker) stays opt-in.

**2586 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed** — 97.18% coverage, gate met.

## The two tests

Both pass. They were never broken — `test_custom_sql_gx.py` needs a live SQL backend (GX's `UnexpectedRowsExpectation` is SQL-only), and `conftest.py` builds the URL from your `.env` Postgres creds, so with the DB down it *attempts* a connection instead of skipping.

## What the exercise actually turned up

The more useful finding is how weak the earlier local runs were:

| Run | Services up | Passed | Skipped | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before | none | 1642 | **943** | 0 (2 errors) |
| Postgres only | pg | 2582 | 2 | **3** |
| Both | pg + redis | **2586** | 1 | **0** |

Starting Postgres moved ~940 tests from *skipped* to *actually executing* — about a third of the backend suite had been silently not running. Then three of those newly-live tests failed for a **second** missing service: Redis backs the SecretStore, so `secret_store.set()` raised `SecretWriteError` → `ConnectionSecretWriteError`. Two layers of environmental skip, each hiding the next.

That's the same shape as the lesson already in your project notes — *a test that cannot express the failing case proves nothing*. Here the tests could express it fine; they just never ran, and the summary line said "passed" either way. A local run with the stack down reports green over a suite that is a third dark, which is exactly the failure mode the "verify locally before pushing" rule exists to prevent.

## State

- `main` clean and current; 0 open PRs, 0 CodeQL alerts, 0 Dependabot alerts.
- conda env synced — all 35 pins match, `pip check` clean, full suite green on it.
- pnpm was already current.
- `dataq-postgres-1` and `dataq-redis-1` are **still running** — I left them up since they're needed for a meaningful local test run. `docker compose down` if you want them stopped.
- Monaco worker bloat filed as [#976](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/976).

One thing I'd suggest, though I haven't done it: `scripts/test-backend.sh` presumably handles bringing the stack up, but a bare `pytest` — which is what editors and I both run — degrades to a third-coverage pass with no warning. A loud notice when `TEST_DATABASE_URL` resolves but the connection fails would turn that silent degradation into a visible one. Say the word and I'll file or implement it.

cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ; gh issue create --title "A bare \`pytest\` silently degrades to a third-coverage run when the compose stack is down" --label "test,priority/P2" --milestone "v1.1 Week 5 — anomaly monitor kind + metric trends" --body "## The problem

With the local compose stack down, \`pytest backend/tests -q\` prints:

\`\`\`
1642 passed, 943 skipped, 5 warnings
\`\`\`

With Postgres and Redis up, the same command on the same commit prints:

\`\`\`
2586 passed, 1 skipped, 5 warnings
\`\`\`

**~940 tests — roughly a third of the backend suite — silently do not run**, and the summary line still reads as success. The skip *reasons* are good and actionable (\`conftest.py\` says \"start it with \`docker compose up -d postgres redis\`\"), but they are only rendered with \`-rs\`, which nobody passes by default. A skip count on its own is indistinguishable from the ~940 live-datasource tests that legitimately skip without credentials.

## Why it bites

The working agreement is to verify locally before pushing rather than lean on CI ([[feedback_verify_locally_before_push]]). A bare \`pytest\` is what editors' test runners invoke (VS Code / PyCharm call pytest directly, not \`scripts/test-backend.sh\`) — and it is what I ran. Green over a suite that is a third dark makes \"I verified locally\" mean much less than it appears to, without anyone noticing.

## It layers, which is the nastier part

Bringing up **only Postgres** does not fix it — it moves ~940 tests from *skipped* to *executing*, and then **three of them fail** against a second missing service:

\`\`\`
backend/app/services/connection_service.py:227: ConnectionSecretWriteError
[info] secret_store_initialized  backend=redis
[warning] connection_secret_write_failed  env=dev type=snowflake
\`\`\`

The SecretStore resolves to the Redis backend (via \`SECRET_STORE\` in \`.env.app\`), so \`secret_store.set()\` raises \`SecretWriteError\`. Two layers of environmental degradation, each hiding the next — and the first layer's skip concealed the second layer's failure entirely.

## What to change

Keep the skip behaviour — running the pure-unit suite anywhere is deliberate (\`conftest.py\` resolution order, point 3). Make the degradation **loud** instead of silent:

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Local test-infra visibility (#977)
#
# Skipping when the compose stack is down is deliberate (resolution order above,
# point 3) — but it must never be QUIET. With the stack down a bare `pytest -q`
# reports "1642 passed, 943 skipped"; with it up, the same commit reports "2586
# passed, 1 skipped". About a third of the suite silently does not run, and the
# summary line reads as success either way.
#
# The per-test skip reasons are already good, but pytest only renders them under
# `-rs`, and a bare skip count is indistinguishable from the live-datasource
# tests that legitimately skip without credentials. Editors (VS Code, PyCharm)
# invoke pytest directly rather than scripts/test-backend.sh, so this is the
# common path, not an edge case.
#
# These hooks report the condition up front and again, loudly, at the end. They
# are visibility only: probes are cheap, failures are swallowed, and nothing here
# can fail a run. In CI both services are up, so the warning never fires.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S = 1.5
_FIX_HINT = "docker compose up -d postgres redis  (or scripts/test-backend.sh)"


def _probe_postgres() -> str | None:
    """None when the test DB is reachable, else a short human reason."""
    if not TEST_DATABASE_URL:
        return "no TEST_DATABASE_URL and no local .env Postgres creds"
    try:
        from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text

        engine = create_engine(
            TEST_DATABASE_URL,
            future=True,
            connect_args={"connect_timeout": int(_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S)},
        )
        try:
            with engine.connect() as conn:
                conn.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
        finally:
            engine.dispose()
    except Exception:
        return "not reachable"
    return None


def _probe_secret_store() -> tuple[str, str | None]:
    """(backend_name, reason_unavailable). Only the redis backend can be *down* —
    `env` is in-process and `azure_key_vault` is never used by the local suite."""
    try:
        settings = get_settings()
        mode = settings.secret_store
    except Exception:
        return ("unknown", None)
    if mode != "redis":
        return (mode, None)
    try:
        import redis

        client = redis.Redis.from_url(
            settings.redis_url,
            socket_connect_timeout=_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S,
            socket_timeout=_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S,
        )
        try:
            client.ping()
        finally:
            client.close()
    except Exception:
        return (mode, "not reachable")
    return (mode, None)


def _infra_status() -> list[tuple[str, str | None]]:
    """[(label, reason_unavailable)] — cached for the session."""
    global _INFRA_STATUS_CACHE
    if _INFRA_STATUS_CACHE is None:
        store_mode, store_reason = _probe_secret_store()
        _INFRA_STATUS_CACHE = [
            ("postgres (test DB)", _probe_postgres()),
            (f"secret store ({store_mode})", store_reason),
        ]
    return _INFRA_STATUS_CACHE


_INFRA_STATUS_CACHE: list[tuple[str, str | None]] | None = None


def pytest_report_header() -> list[str]:
    """State infra reachability before the run, so a degraded pass is visible
    from the first line rather than inferred from a skip count at the end."""
    lines = []
    for label, reason in _infra_status():
        lines.append(f"test infra: {label} — {'OK' if reason is None else reason.upper()}")
    if any(reason for _, reason in _infra_status()):
        lines.append(f"test infra: DEGRADED — DB-backed tests will skip. Fix: {_FIX_HINT}")
    return lines


def pytest_terminal_summary(terminalreporter: object) -> None:
    """Re-state a degraded run at the end, where the summary line is read.

    The header scrolls away on a long run; this is the part that stops a
    third-coverage pass from being mistaken for a green one.
    """
    down = [(label, reason) for label, reason in _infra_status() if reason]
    if not down:
        return
    skipped = len(terminalreporter.stats.get("skipped", []))  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    write = terminalreporter.write_line  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
    write("")
    write("!" * 79, red=True, bold=True)
    write("DEGRADED RUN — this suite did NOT fully execute.", red=True, bold=True)
    for label, reason in down:
        write(f"  unavailable: {label} — {reason}", red=True)
    write(f"  {skipped} test(s) skipped; the DB-backed tests are among them.", red=True)
    write(f"  Fix: {_FIX_HINT}", red=True, bold=True)
    write("A pass here does not mean what a full local run means.", red=True)
    write("!" * 79, red=True, bold=True)

Issue [#977](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/977) filed, fix implemented and verified across all four states. Full suite running before I commit.

Verification so far:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| All healthy, no `-q` | Header: `postgres — OK`, `secret store (redis) — OK` |
| All healthy, `-q` | **No banner** — stays quiet when it should |
| Postgres down, `-q` | Banner fires: *"1 test(s) skipped — the DB-backed tests are among them"* |
| Redis down, `-q` | Banner fires: *"1 test(s) failed/errored — likely for this reason, not a code defect"* |

The `-q` cases matter most: `pytest_report_header` is suppressed under `-q`, so the header alone would have missed the exact mode that hid the problem. The `pytest_terminal_summary` banner is what actually closes it.

`backend/tests/conftest.py` only (commit `65e18a67`, `git diff origin/main...HEAD`). I ran the hooks live under the pinned pytest 9.1.1 in the `dataq` conda env, in four configurations: DB up, DB down, DB pointed at a non-postgres driver, and DB pointed at a blackhole IP.

## Important (80-89)

**1. The banner prints *above* the coverage table, so on the actual command it scrolls off — 90**
`/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/tests/conftest.py:308` (`pytest_terminal_summary`)

Conftest hookimpls are registered last and therefore called *first*, before pytest-cov's own `pytest_terminal_summary`. The repo's `addopts` includes `--cov-report=term-missing`, so on a real run the banner lands ~140 lines from the end. Measured on a degraded run of one file:

```
7:DEGRADED RUN — local test infrastructure was unavailable.
14:______________ coverage: platform darwin ... ____________
149:FAIL Required test coverage of 80% not reached. Total coverage: 8.27%
150:3 skipped in 0.66s
```

On the full suite the term-missing table is far longer. This defeats the stated purpose ("Re-state a degraded run at the end, where the summary line is read"). Fix — verified, moves the banner to line 144, directly above the final summary:

```python
@pytest.hookimpl(trylast=True)
def pytest_terminal_summary(terminalreporter: object) -> None:
```

**2. The header never renders under `-q`, which is the command in the issue — 85**
`/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/tests/conftest.py:293` (`pytest_report_header`)

pytest's `TerminalReporter` gates all header output on `showheader = verbosity >= 0`; `-q` sets verbosity `-1`. Verified: the three `test infra:` lines appear on plain `pytest` and are absent on `pytest -q` (the probes still run, the output is discarded). The docstring's claim — "visible from the first line rather than inferred from a skip count at the end" — is therefore false for the exact invocation the module comment cites ("a bare `pytest -q` reports 1642 passed, 943 skipped"). Combined with finding 1, `pytest -q` today shows *neither* half where it can be seen. Fixing 1 makes the summary the reliable channel; the header comment should be softened to note it is a non-`-q` affordance.

**3. `connect_args={"connect_timeout": ...}` makes a working DB report "not reachable" — 85**
`/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/tests/conftest.py:236-247` (`_probe_postgres`)

The kwarg is psycopg2/psycopg-specific. Any other driver in an explicit `TEST_DATABASE_URL` raises `TypeError: 'connect_timeout' is an invalid keyword argument` at connect time, which the bare `except Exception` swallows and converts into `"not reachable"`. Verified with `TEST_DATABASE_URL=sqlite:///…`:

```
test infra: postgres (test DB) — NOT REACHABLE
test infra: DEGRADED — DB-backed tests will skip. ...
```

The DB was perfectly reachable. The probe cannot distinguish "server down" from "probe could not run", so it emits a false DEGRADED claim — the same class of untrue-status defect the PR's own comment ("Claiming skips on a run that had none would be the exact defect this banner exists to prevent") sets out to avoid. Suggested fix: only attach `connect_args` when `make_url(TEST_DATABASE_URL).drivername.startswith("postgresql+psycopg")`, or catch `TypeError`/`ArgumentError` separately and report `"probe unavailable"` rather than `"not reachable"`.

**4. No test covers any of the new logic — 80**

The diff adds ~140 lines of branching (three probe outcomes, four banner variants, the cache) with no test, against CLAUDE.md §6 step 2 and the standing "mutation-check every regression test" habit. `backend/tests/conftest.py` is outside `--cov=backend/app`, so the 80% gate cannot see the gap either. pytest's `pytester` fixture makes this directly testable (run an inline suite with `TEST_DATABASE_URL` pointed at a dead port and assert on `result.stdout`), and such a test would have caught findings 1 and 3.

## Minor (noted, not blocking)

- `int(_PROBE_TIMEOUT_S)` truncates 1.5 → 1, and libpq silently clamps `connect_timeout < 2` to 2 — the effective budget is 2s, not the 1.5s the constant advertises.
- `"{n} test(s) skipped — the DB-backed tests are among them."` is asserted whenever anything skipped, including when only the secret store is down, or when the selected tests skipped for missing live-datasource credentials with no DB-backed test in the selection.
- `_probe_secret_store`'s redis branch only runs when `settings.secret_store == "redis"`; the redis-touching tests in the suite stub the client, so the line is informational rather than a coverage signal. Not wrong, just narrower than the label suggests.
- Asked-about non-issues: nothing here touches the pytest cache, so `-p no:cacheprovider` is inert; xdist is not a dependency, and if installed the only effect is one extra probe per worker (the summary runs on the controller, which also probes).

"""The degraded-run banner in conftest (#977).

These guard a piece of *diagnostic* code, which is exactly the kind that rots
unnoticed: nothing else fails when it goes wrong, so the only signal is a
person mistaking a third-coverage run for a green one — the failure this
banner exists to prevent.

Two of the three defects these lock down survived a manual four-state
walkthrough of the feature. `trylast` was missed because every hand-check
passed `--no-cov`, so the coverage table that buries the banner was never
rendered; the psycopg-only `connect_args` was missed because every hand-check
used a postgres URL. Both are cases the manual test could not express.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any

import backend.tests.conftest as conftest


class _FakeReporter:
    """Stands in for pytest's TerminalReporter, capturing written lines."""

    def __init__(self, **stats: list[object]) -> None:
        self.stats: dict[str, list[object]] = stats
        self.lines: list[str] = []

    def write_line(self, line: str, **_: Any) -> None:
        self.lines.append(line)


def _banner(monkeypatch: Any, status: list[tuple[str, str | None]], **stats: list[object]) -> str:
    monkeypatch.setattr(conftest, "_INFRA_STATUS_CACHE", status)
    reporter = _FakeReporter(**stats)
    conftest.pytest_terminal_summary(reporter)
    return "\n".join(reporter.lines)


# --- the banner fires only when it should ----------------------------------


def test_healthy_infra_prints_nothing(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """A quiet gate is the whole point — noise on a healthy run trains people
    to ignore it, which is how the banner would stop working."""
    out = _banner(monkeypatch, [("postgres (test DB)", None), ("secret store (env)", None)])
    assert out == ""


def test_degraded_infra_names_the_service_and_the_fix(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    out = _banner(
        monkeypatch,
        [("postgres (test DB)", "not reachable"), ("secret store (redis)", None)],
        skipped=[object()],
    )
    assert "DEGRADED RUN" in out
    assert "postgres (test DB) — not reachable" in out
    assert "docker compose up -d postgres redis" in out
    # The healthy service must not be listed as unavailable.
    assert "secret store (redis) —" not in out


# --- the banner claims only what happened ----------------------------------
#
# A missing Postgres makes tests SKIP; a missing secret store makes them FAIL.
# Reporting one as the other would be the same untrue-status defect the banner
# is meant to catch.


def test_skips_are_reported_as_skips_not_failures(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    out = _banner(
        monkeypatch,
        [("postgres (test DB)", "not reachable")],
        skipped=[object(), object()],
    )
    assert "2 test(s) skipped" in out
    assert "failed/errored" not in out


def test_failures_are_reported_as_failures_not_skips(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """Regression: an early draft printed "0 test(s) skipped" on this path."""
    out = _banner(
        monkeypatch,
        [("secret store (redis)", "not reachable")],
        failed=[object()],
        error=[object()],
    )
    assert "2 test(s) failed/errored" in out
    assert "skipped" not in out


def test_neither_skips_nor_failures_still_warns_without_inventing_counts(
    monkeypatch: Any,
) -> None:
    out = _banner(monkeypatch, [("secret store (redis)", "not reachable")])
    assert "DEGRADED RUN" in out
    assert "test(s) skipped" not in out
    assert "test(s) failed" not in out


# --- ordering: the banner must survive the coverage table ------------------


def test_terminal_summary_is_trylast() -> None:
    """Without ``trylast``, this hook runs BEFORE pytest-cov's summary and the
    banner prints above a ~140-line term-missing table — scrolling off exactly
    like the header it backs up. Verified by hand: banner at line 6, real
    summary at line 149. This is a behavioural requirement, not a style choice.
    """
    opts = getattr(conftest.pytest_terminal_summary, "pytest_impl", {})
    assert opts.get("trylast") is True


# --- the probe must not cry wolf -------------------------------------------


def test_probe_does_not_claim_unreachable_for_a_non_psycopg_driver(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """``connect_timeout`` is libpq-specific. Passing it to another driver raises
    at connect time; swallowing that into "not reachable" would report a healthy
    database as down.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(conftest, "TEST_DATABASE_URL", "sqlite://")  # in-memory, always up
    assert conftest._probe_postgres() is None


def test_probe_reports_a_genuinely_dead_postgres(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    """The other half: a real postgres URL pointing nowhere must still be caught,
    so the wolf-guard above cannot silence a true alarm.
    """
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        conftest,
        "TEST_DATABASE_URL",
        "REDACTED",
    )
    assert conftest._probe_postgres() == "not reachable"


def test_probe_without_a_url_explains_itself(monkeypatch: Any) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(conftest, "TEST_DATABASE_URL", None)
    reason = conftest._probe_postgres()
    assert reason is not None and "TEST_DATABASE_URL" in reason

The review found four real defects and two of them were things my own verification structurally could not catch. Full suite running; I'll push once it's green.

The important one: **`trylast` was missing**, so the banner printed *above* pytest-cov's ~140-line coverage table and scrolled off — defeating the entire purpose. I missed it because every one of my four hand-checks passed `--no-cov`, so the table that buries it never rendered. Same shape as the `connect_args` bug: I only ever probed with a postgres URL, so I never saw that a non-psycopg driver makes a healthy database report `NOT REACHABLE` — a false alarm from the banner built to prevent false claims.

Both are now locked down by tests, and I mutation-checked each: removing `trylast` fails `test_terminal_summary_is_trylast`, restoring the unconditional `connect_args` fails `test_probe_does_not_claim_unreachable_for_a_non_psycopg_driver`.
